entity.contextDescription: The model prayer taught by our Lord Jesus Christ (Matthew 6:9–13)

prayerPoint.title: The Lord's Prayer
prayerPoint.description:
Our Father, who is in heaven,
May your Name be honoured. May your kingdom come. May your will be done on earth, as it is in heaven.

Give us today our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us. And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil:

For yours is the kingdom, the power, and the glory, for ever and ever. Amen.

entity.contextDescription: Historic Anglican collect from the 1662 Book of Common Prayer (Morning Prayer)

prayerPoint.title: Collect for Peace
prayerPoint.description:
O God, author of peace and lover of concord, to know you is our eternal life, and to serve you is perfect freedom;

Defend us, your humble servants, from all assaults of our enemies; that we, surely trusting in your defence, may not fear the power of any adversaries, through the might of Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen.

entity.contextDescription: Historic Anglican collect from the 1662 Book of Common Prayer (Morning Prayer)

prayerPoint.title: Collect for Grace
prayerPoint.description:
O Lord, our heavenly Father, Almighty and everlasting God, who have safely brought us to the beginning of this day;

Defend us today with your mighty power; and grant that today we fall into no sin, neither run into any kind of danger; but that all we do may be ordered by your governance, to always do what is righteous in your sight; through Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen.

entity.contextDescription: Historic Anglican collect from the 1662 Book of Common Prayer (Holy Communion)

prayerPoint.title: Collect for Purity
prayerPoint.description:
Almighty God, to whom all hearts are open, all desires known, and from whom no secrets are hidden;

Cleanse the thoughts of our hearts by the inspiration of your Holy Spirit, that we may love you perfectly, and worthily magnify your holy Name; through Christ our Lord. Amen.

entity.contextDescription: Composed by Bishop Edward Reynolds for the 1662 Book of Common Prayer

prayerPoint.title: A General Thanksgiving
prayerPoint.description:
Almighty God, Father of all mercies, we your unworthy servants give you most humble and hearty thanks for all your goodness and loving-kindness to us, and to all people.

We bless you for our creation, preservation, and all the blessings of this life; but above all, for your inestimable love in the redemption of the world by our Lord Jesus Christ; for the means of grace, and for the hope of glory.

And, we ask you, give us a due sense of all your mercies, that our hearts may be truly thankful, and that we show your praise, not only with our lips, but in our lives; by giving ourselves to your service, and by walking before you in holiness and righteousness all our days; through Jesus Christ our Lord, to whom with you and the Holy Spirit be all honour and glory, world without end. Amen.

entity.contextDescription: Historic ecumenical confession of the Christian faith (Thirty-Nine Articles, Art. VIII)

prayerPoint.title: The Apostles' Creed
prayerPoint.description:
I believe in God the Father Almighty, Maker of heaven and earth:

And in Jesus Christ his only Son our Lord, who was conceived by the Holy Spirit, born of the Virgin Mary, suffered under Pontius Pilate, was crucified, dead, and buried: he descended into hell; the third day he rose again from the dead; he ascended into heaven, and sits at the right hand of God the Father Almighty; from there he will come to judge the living and the dead.

I believe in the Holy Spirit; the holy Catholic Church; the communion of saints; the forgiveness of sins; the resurrection of the body, and the life everlasting. Amen.

entity.contextDescription: Pulpit prayer at the Metropolitan Tabernacle (Passmore & Alabaster, 1905, Prayer I)

prayerPoint.title: Help from on High
prayerPoint.description:
You who are King of kings and Lord of lords,
we worship you.
We can truly say that we delight in God;
our longing is to feel your presence,
and where you are is heaven itself.

Come near, our Father,
come very near to your children.
Some of us are very weak in body and faint in heart;
lay your right hand upon us, and say to us, 'Do not fear.'

Lord Jesus, take away from us now
everything that would hinder close communion with God.
Our highest prayer is for perfect holiness,
complete consecration,
and entire cleansing from every evil.

Take our hearts, our minds, our hands, and our feet,
and use all of us for yourself.
We ask in the name of Jesus Christ your Son. Amen.

entity.contextDescription: Pulpit prayer at the Metropolitan Tabernacle (Passmore & Alabaster, 1905, Prayer VIII)

prayerPoint.title: A Prayer for Holiness
prayerPoint.description:
Our Father, we worship and love you;
and a central part of our worship is that you are holy.
Teach us to love goodness, purity, justice,
and true holiness.

O God, do not let us live in vain.
Cleanse us from secret faults,
and keep your servants from willful sins;
let them not rule over us.
Work in us to will and to do what pleases you.

May the life of Christ shine in our lives,
so that others may see we have been with Jesus,
and have learned from him.
We ask all through Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen.

entity.contextDescription: Pulpit prayer at the Metropolitan Tabernacle (Passmore & Alabaster, 1905, Prayer II)

prayerPoint.title: Thanks Be To God
prayerPoint.description:
O Lord God,
help us now to truly worship you.
Shut the door on the world for us;
help us to forget our cares.
Lift us completely above this world,
and take away all its downward pull.

O precious Lord Jesus Christ,
we adore you with all our hearts.
You gave your life for your people;
you ransomed us with your lifeblood.
Be forever beloved and adored.

Unite our hearts with yours,
and be our heart and soul,
our life and everything to us.

Reign, Immanuel, reign;
sit upon your high throne,
and let Christ alone reign. Amen.

entity.contextDescription: Pulpit prayer at the Metropolitan Tabernacle (Passmore & Alabaster, 1905, Prayer III)

prayerPoint.title: The Love Without Measure
prayerPoint.description:
Lord, we long to come to you,
but come to us.
Draw us, and we will run after you.
Blessed Spirit, help our weakness,
for we do not know how to pray as we ought.

We thank you, Lord,
for the everlasting love that chose us before the earth was made;
for the boundless love that entered into covenant for our redemption;
for the unfailing love that appeared in the person of Christ and accomplished our salvation;
and for that love which has never changed, though we have wandered.

Complete your work within our hearts.
Grant that we may abide in Christ and live close to God,
through Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen.

entity.contextDescription: Pulpit prayer at the Metropolitan Tabernacle (Passmore & Alabaster, 1905, Prayer IV)

prayerPoint.title: The All-Prevailing Plea
prayerPoint.description:
O Lord God, the fountain of all fullness,
we, who are nothing but emptiness,
come to you for every need;
and we will not come in vain,
since we bring with us a plea that always prevails.

We come at the command of your Word,
encouraged by your promise,
and led by Christ Jesus, our great High Priest.

To you be glory and honour,
power and majesty,
dominion and might,
forever and ever!

Refresh every corner of your vineyard,
and let the dew of heaven rest on every branch of the vine.
Bless your church throughout the world,
and come quickly, Lord Jesus. Amen.

entity.contextDescription: Pulpit prayer at the Metropolitan Tabernacle (Passmore & Alabaster, 1905, Prayer XI)

prayerPoint.title: Under the Blood
prayerPoint.description:
Lord our God,
we thank you that the record of your covenant faithfulness remains.
You keep your promises, and your Word never fails.
We bless you that our sins are blotted out
by the atoning sacrifice of Jesus.

For all our wanderings,
for all our shortcomings,
for all our unfaithfulness,
forgive us, O Lord,
and wash us clean in the precious blood of the Lamb.

Grant us grace to walk worthily of our high calling in Christ Jesus,
keeping ourselves unstained by the world.
In the name of our Saviour, Jesus Christ. Amen.

entity.contextDescription: Pulpit prayer at the Metropolitan Tabernacle (Passmore & Alabaster, 1905, Prayer XV)

prayerPoint.title: The Peace of God
prayerPoint.description:
Our God,
we do not stand far off as Israel did at Sinai,
and no dark veil hangs between your face and ours;
for the veil was torn by the death of our divine Lord and Mediator, Jesus Christ.
In his name we come to the mercy seat,
and here we present our prayers and our praises,
accepted in him.

Grant us the peace of God, which surpasses all understanding.
Quiet our hearts in your own love;
let no worldly care disturb the deep calm of our spirits in Christ Jesus.

To him who loved us
and washed us from our sins in his own blood,
be glory forever. Amen.

entity.contextDescription: Pulpit prayer at the Metropolitan Tabernacle (Passmore & Alabaster, 1905, Prayer XX)

prayerPoint.title: The Great Sacrifice

entity.displayName: A Morning Prayer (Syrian Clementine Liturgy, 1st c.)
entity.contextDescription: Syrian Clementine Liturgy, first century (Potts, Prayers of the Early Church)

prayerPoint.title: A Morning Prayer

entity.contextDescription: Clement of Rome, first century (Potts, Prayers of the Early Church)

prayerPoint.title: For Rulers and Governors
prayerPoint.description:
To our rulers and governors on earth, to them you, Lord, gave the power of the kingdom by your glorious and unspeakable might, so that we may know the glory and honour given to them by you, and be subject to them, in nothing resisting your will.

To them, Lord, give health, peace, concord and stability, so that they may exercise the authority given to them without offence. For you, O heavenly Lord and eternal King, give to us all glory and honour and power over the things on earth; Lord, direct their counsel toward what is good and pleasing in your sight, so that, in peace and gentleness, exercising with reverence the power given by you, they may find you favourable.

You alone can do these things and still greater good for us; we praise you through the High Priest and Guardian of our souls, Jesus Christ, through whom be glory and majesty to you, both now and from generation to generation, for evermore. Amen.

entity.contextDescription: The Clementine Liturgy, first century (Potts, Prayers of the Early Church)

prayerPoint.title: A Pure Heart
prayerPoint.description: O God Almighty, Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, your only begotten Son, give me a blameless body, a pure heart, a watchful mind and a right understanding, and the presence of your Holy Spirit, so that I may gain and always hold firmly to an unshaken faith in your truth, through Jesus Christ, your Son, our Lord; through whom be glory to you in the Holy Spirit, for ever and ever. Amen.

entity.contextDescription: Polycarp, second century (Potts, Prayers of the Early Church)

prayerPoint.title: Intercession
prayerPoint.description:
May God the Father, and the eternal High Priest Jesus Christ, build us up in faith and truth and love, and grant us our portion among the saints, with all those who believe in our Lord Jesus Christ.

We pray for all believers, for kings and rulers, for the enemies of the cross of Christ, and for ourselves we pray that our fruit may abound, and that we may be made perfect in Christ Jesus our Lord. Amen.

entity.contextDescription: The Martyrdom of Polycarp, second century (Potts, Prayers of the Early Church)

prayerPoint.title: A Dying Prayer
prayerPoint.description:
O Father of your well-beloved and blessed Son Jesus Christ, through whom we have known you; O God of the angels and powers and of every living creature, and of all the righteous who live in your presence,

I thank you that you have graciously brought me to this day and this hour, to receive a portion among the number of martyrs, among the people of Christ, to the resurrection of everlasting life, both of body and soul, in the incorruption of the Holy Spirit. Receive me today in your sight as a fruitful and acceptable sacrifice, as you before prepared, often revealed and now fulfilled, most faithful God who cannot lie.

Therefore for all things I praise you, I bless you, I glorify you, through the everlasting High Priest, Jesus Christ, your well-beloved Son, to whom with you and the Holy Spirit be all glory, world without end. Amen.

entity.displayName: For a Pure Heart (Liturgy of St James, 2nd c.)
entity.contextDescription: Liturgy of St James, second century (Potts, Prayers of the Early Church)

prayerPoint.title: For a Pure Heart

entity.displayName: For Right Blessings (Basil the Great, 4th c.)
entity.contextDescription: Basil the Great, fourth century (Potts, Prayers of the Early Church)

prayerPoint.title: For Right Blessings
prayerPoint.description:
O Lord our God, teach us, we pray, to ask you rightly for the right blessings. Steer the vessel of our life toward yourself, you calm harbour of all storm-tossed souls. Show us the course we should take.

Renew a willing spirit within us. Let your Spirit restrain our wandering senses, and guide us and enable us toward what is truly good, to keep your laws, and in all our work always to rejoice in your glorious and gladdening presence.

For yours is the glory and praise from all your saints, for ever and ever. Amen.

entity.displayName: For Two or Three (John Chrysostom, 4th c.)
entity.contextDescription: John Chrysostom, fourth century (Potts, Prayers of the Early Church)

prayerPoint.title: For Two or Three
prayerPoint.description:
Almighty God, who have given us grace at this time to make our common prayers to you; and promise that when two or three are gathered together in your name you will grant their requests:

Fulfil now, O Lord, the desires and petitions of your servants, as may be best for them, granting us in this world knowledge of your truth, and in the world to come, life everlasting. Amen.

entity.contextDescription: Ambrose of Milan, fourth century (Potts, Prayers of the Early Church)

prayerPoint.title: For Pardon
prayerPoint.description:
O Lord, who has mercy on all, take away my sins from me, and kindly kindle in me the fire of your Holy Spirit.

Take away from me the heart of stone, and give me a heart of flesh, a heart to love and adore you, a heart to delight in you, to follow and to enjoy you, for Christ's sake. Amen.

entity.contextDescription: Nerses of Clajes, fourth century (Potts, Prayers of the Early Church)

prayerPoint.title: For Protection
prayerPoint.description:
Lord Jesus Christ, keeper and preserver of all things, let your right hand guard us by day and by night, when we sit at home and when we walk abroad, when we lie down and when we rise up, so that we may be kept from all evil.

Have mercy on us sinners. Amen.

entity.contextDescription: Augustine of Hippo (Potts, Prayers of the Early Church)

prayerPoint.title: For Steadfastness
prayerPoint.description:
O God, the light of every heart that sees you, the life of every soul that loves you, the strength of every mind that seeks you, grant me always to remain steadfast in your holy love.

Be the joy of my heart; take it wholly to yourself, and dwell there.

The house of my soul, I confess, is too narrow for you; enlarge it, so that you may enter in. It is broken down, but repair it. There is much within it that must offend your eyes; I confess and know it.

But whose help shall I ask in cleansing it, but yours alone? To you, therefore, I cry urgently, asking that you would cleanse me from my secret faults, and keep your servant from presumptuous sins, so that they never rule over me. Amen.

entity.contextDescription: Attributed to Augustine of Hippo (Potts, Prayers of the Early Church)

prayerPoint.title: Evening Prayer
prayerPoint.description:
Watch, dear Lord, with those who wake, or watch, or weep tonight, and give your angels charge over those who sleep.
Tend your sick ones, O Lord Christ. Rest your weary ones. Bless your dying ones.
Soothe your suffering ones. Pity your afflicted ones. Shield your joyous ones.

And all, for your love's sake. Amen.

entity.contextDescription: Augustine of Hippo (Potts, Prayers of the Early Church)

prayerPoint.title: Praise
prayerPoint.description: Great are you, O Lord, and greatly to be praised; great is your power, and your wisdom has no end. We long to praise you without ceasing. You call us to delight in your praise, for you have made us for yourself, and our hearts find no rest until they rest in you; to whom with the Father and the Holy Spirit be all glory, praise and honour, both now and for evermore. Amen.

entity.contextDescription: Leonine Sacramentary, fifth century (Potts, Prayers of the Early Church)

prayerPoint.title: For Right Living
prayerPoint.description: Grant to us, Lord, we pray, the spirit to think and do always what is right; so that we, who cannot do anything good without you, may be enabled by you to live according to your will; through Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen.

entity.displayName: For Love of God (Gelasian Sacramentary, 5th c.)
entity.contextDescription: Gelasian Sacramentary, fifth century (Potts, Prayers of the Early Church)

prayerPoint.title: For Love of God
prayerPoint.description: O God, who have prepared for those who love you such good things as pass our understanding; pour into our hearts such love toward you, that we, loving you above all things, may obtain your promises, which exceed all that we can desire; through Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen.

entity.contextDescription: Gelasian Sacramentary, fifth century (Potts, Prayers of the Early Church)

prayerPoint.title: To Serve You
prayerPoint.description: O God, the light of the minds that know you, the life of the souls that love you, the strength of the thoughts that seek you, help us to know you so that we may truly love you, and to love you so that we may fully serve you, whose service is perfect freedom; through Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen.
